# Buyer Quirk Sheet — Department of Water and Sanitation

**Buyer:** Department of Water and Sanitation (national dept), including its Construction South / Construction East regional units and the Vaal‑Orange Catchment Management Agency (VOCMA), which procures on DWS SBD templates and via dws.gov.za contacts
**Kind:** National department (with a subordinate catchment management agency)
**Packs sampled:** 10 — ocds-9t57fa-165781, ocds-9t57fa-164860, ocds-9t57fa-165775, ocds-9t57fa-164876, ocds-9t57fa-165776, ocds-9t57fa-164869, ocds-9t57fa-165939, ocds-9t57fa-165951, ocds-9t57fa-164290, ocds-9t57fa-165885
**Date:** 2026-08

Note on the corpus: 8 of the 10 packs are DWS goods/works quotations and RFBs (plywood shutter board, river sand, plaster sand, ready-mix concrete, dump-truck hire, excavator hire, water-quality meter RFQ); 2 (ocds-9t57fa-165939, ocds-9t57fa-165951) are VOCMA Requests for Bid (recruitment agency, internal audit services); ocds-9t57fa-164290 is a standalone, DWS-unbranded copy of the National Treasury GCC (July 2010) with no bid number or DWS references — treated as reference boilerplate, not a distinctive DWS clause, and excluded from buyer-specific claims below except where noted.

---

## Submission channel & rules

- **Hard-copy bid box is the default and, for the formal SBD-based bids, the only channel.** Construction-materials/plant-hire tenders instruct: "BID RESPONSE DOCUMENTS MAY BE SUBMITTED IN BID BOX TO: ... The bid box at the entrance of Department Water and Sanitation Mthatha Dam Office Building" (ocds-9t57fa-165781, also 165775, 165776) and "deposit in the bid box at the entrance of 4-6 Alkmaar Street, Daljosaphat, Paarl" (ocds-9t57fa-164876, similarly 164860, 164869).
- **Electronic submission is explicitly barred for these tenders**: "No bid forwarded by telegram, telex, facsimile or email will be considered. Only bids deposited in bid box will be acceptable on closing date before or at 11:00" (ocds-9t57fa-165781; identical wording in 164860, 164876, 165775, 165776, 164869).
- **Sealing/labeling is mandatory and prescriptive**: "The original Bid, together with a covering letter and supporting documents, shall be sealed in an envelope endorsed: 'Original Bid: WTE1032CE: SUPPLY AND DELIVERY OF LOCAL CONTENT PLYWOOD SHUTTER BOARD...'" (ocds-9t57fa-165781); "sealed in an envelope endorsed: 'ORIGINAL BID FOR BID: WTE-0546 CS...' and the name of the Bidder shall be clearly shown" (ocds-9t57fa-164876).
- **Low-value RFQs run a dual channel instead**: the water-quality-meter-kit RFQ states "Submit via email: Gumedes2@dws.gov.za / Nkabindev@dws.gov.za" as well as listing the bid box (ocds-9t57fa-165885) — email is acceptable here even though the identical-looking SBD1 boilerplate a few lines above still says bid-box-only, i.e. the RFQ cover sheet overrides the standard SBD1 text for this specific quotation.
- **VOCMA (the catchment agency) advertises via e-Tenders but still requires physical delivery**: cover pages list "e-Tenders Portal" as the response address (ocds-9t57fa-165939, ocds-9t57fa-165951), yet the terms and conditions later state "All bid documents should be hand delivered and deposited into the Tender Box, if sent via post, envelope or package, the envelope must be clearly marked to avoid your submission been mixed with normal letters sent to the Agency. Only signed, original documents will be accepted" (ocds-9t57fa-165951, same text in 165939) — e-Tenders is the advertising/download portal, not a valid submission channel.
- No dual-channel "hard-copy governs over electronic" tie-break rule was found (no clause addresses what happens if both a hard copy and an electronic copy are lodged) — Not observed in sampled packs.

## Municipal-arrears / rates clause

Not observed in sampled packs. None of the 10 packs contain any clause on municipal rates, service-charge arrears, or a "not more than X days in arrears" test for bidders or directors. Municipal-arrears screening does not appear to be part of this buyer's standard mandatory-document set (contrast with buyers who bake COJ/municipal-arrears certificates into their SBD1 pack).

## B-BBEE treatment

- **Preference points only — not a pre-qualification gate.** Every SBD6.1 form uses the standard 80/20 system (bids up to R50m): "The applicable preference point system for this tender is the 80/20 preference point system... PRICE 80 / SPECIFIC GOALS 20" (ocds-9t57fa-165885, and equivalently in all construction packs). B‑BBEE contributes 3 of the 20 specific-goals points in the RFQ example ("B-BBEE status level contribution from level 1 to 2 which are QSE or EME — 3" points, ocds-9t57fa-165885) or the full 20 points in the simpler construction-materials packs ("a maximum of 20 points will be awarded for attaining the Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (B-BBEE) Status Level of Contribution," ocds-9t57fa-165781).
- **Non-submission forfeits points, it does not disqualify the bid**: "Complete, sign, and submit SBD 6.1 according to PPR 2022 (failure to submit, the Bidder will forfeit the preferential points to be claimed)" (ocds-9t57fa-165781, and the same construction in 164860, 164869, 164876, 165775, 165776). This is a curable/soft consequence, distinct from the hard mandatory-document disqualifications elsewhere in the same tables.
- Certificates must be current: "B-BBEE certificate must be a certified copy and it must be valid on or before the closing date of the invitation" (ocds-9t57fa-165951).
- No evidence of a hard B‑BBEE-level pre-qualification threshold (e.g. "Level 1-4 only may bid") in any sampled pack — Not observed.
- **Quirk:** the water-quality-meter RFQ pack (ocds-9t57fa-165885) bundles both the scored SBD6.1 preference-points claim (B-BBEE worth real points) and a separate supplier-info table stating B-BBEE data "is for reporting purposes only, and will not prejudice the company in any way nor will it be considered as an evaluation tool" — two inconsistent statements on whether B-BBEE affects the outcome, sitting in the same document.

## Cure/condonation policy

- **VOCMA explicitly allows late/deferred submission of returnable administrative documents** — the only true "cure" clause found in the corpus: "Bidders will not be disqualified at this stage should the returnable administrative documents not be attached; however, should the bidder be recommended all the documents be required prior to the award" (ocds-9t57fa-165939, identical language would apply to 165951's equivalent stage). This is a clear tiering: administrative-document gaps are curable pre-award, but the documents must exist and be produced before contract signature.
- **DWS's own construction/goods packs use a much harder default**: mandatory documents (SBD1, SBD3.1, SBD4, compulsory briefing attendance) are Phase 1 and fatal on the spot — "Failure to complete, sign and submit the documents listed in table 1 below will render your bid non-responsive and will be disqualified" / "Failure to attend compulsory site briefing... will render your bid non-responsive and will be disqualified" (ocds-9t57fa-165781). Specification non-compliance is also fatal without a cure path: "A bidder who fails to comply with the specification requirements... will be disqualified and not considered for further evaluation" (ocds-9t57fa-165781).
- Clarification is permitted only pre-submission, formally, from the buyer's side, never from the bidder correcting its own bid post-submission: "the Bidders must immediately notify the Department in order to have any discrepancy rectified or clarified before submitting his bid. Such clarification will be valid only if made by the Department by means of formal amendment" (ocds-9t57fa-165781, identical in 164860/164876/165775/165776/164869).
- Net picture: this buyer runs two regimes side by side — the standard construction/goods bid packs treat almost everything as fatal (no condonation), while the VOCMA services RFBs explicitly condone missing administrative paperwork up to (but not through) award.

## Security/vetting requirements

- **No post-award security vetting, integrity pact, or lifestyle-audit clause found for the bidding company itself** in any pack — Not observed in sampled packs.
- **POPIA/PAIA consent is required, but only in the VOCMA recruitment-agency RFB**, and it is about the placed candidates, not the bidder's own vetting: "Annexure 6 - POPI Consent forms consent to process (use) personal information (Informed Consent Notice) as per Promotion of Access to Information Act 2 of 2000... and the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA). NB: Should the company be a Joint Venture (JV) both parties must consent and sign this consent form" (ocds-9t57fa-165939).
- The only "vetting" reference in the corpus is a scope-of-work item for the successful recruitment agency to perform on placed job candidates, not a buyer requirement on the bidder: "2.3.6 Conduct the vetting of the successful candidate" (ocds-9t57fa-165939).
- Standard state-employee/conflict-of-interest declarations (SBD4) and the Register of Tender Defaulters check are universal but generic to National Treasury bidding, not distinctive to this buyer: "If a person is listed in the Register for Tender Defaulters and/or the List of Restricted Suppliers, that person will automatically be disqualified from the bid process" (present verbatim across all 8 branded packs, e.g. ocds-9t57fa-165885).

## Financial demands

- **Performance security is explicitly waived for plant-hire and materials-supply contracts** via a filled-in Special Conditions of Contract clause: "7.4 No performance security is required" (ocds-9t57fa-164860 — dump-truck hire; ocds-9t57fa-164869 — excavator hire; ocds-9t57fa-164876 — ready-mix concrete supply). Where the SCC table is left unfilled (river sand, plaster sand, plywood shutter board packs — ocds-9t57fa-165775, 165776, 165781), the position defaults to the generic GCC clause 7 wording without a specific figure, i.e. Not stated as a number in those packs.
- **Insurance requirement for rented plant is a full-replacement-value obligation on the supplier, not a buyer-provided cover**: "The supplier shall, at its own cost, insure the rented equipment for the full replacement value against loss, theft, damage, or destruction for the entire duration of the rental period, including any period the equipment is in transit" (ocds-9t57fa-164860, mirrored in 164869).
- **Compensation Fund / COID letter of good standing is a mandatory administrative document for plant-hire tenders**: "A valid letter of Good Standing with the Compensation Commissioner in terms of the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act No 130 of 1993 and or third parties' insurance registered with Financial Service Board" (ocds-9t57fa-164860, 164869) — this is not required in the pure supply-only packs (river sand, plaster sand, shutter board, ready-mix concrete, RFQ), so it tracks with contracts that put DWS plant/personnel/equipment risk on-site.
- No audited financial statements, bank confirmation letters, or credit-rating requirements were found in any sampled pack as a bidder pre-qualification item — Not observed in sampled packs (the one "financial statements" reference in ocds-9t57fa-165951 is a description of the internal-audit service scope, i.e. what the appointed auditor will review for DWS/VOCMA, not a document demanded from bidders).
- Standard National Treasury GCC 2010 performance-security machinery (bank guarantee/irrevocable letter of credit or certified cheque, lodged within 30 days of award) is attached as boilerplate across the corpus (ocds-9t57fa-164290 and the GCC annexures in every branded pack) but is not itself distinctive to DWS.

## Functionality norms

- **Functionality gates appear only in the VOCMA professional-services RFBs, not in the simple goods/plant-hire quotations.** Internal-audit RFB: "Only Bids that meet the minimum threshold of 70 out of 100 points for functionality will proceed to the next stage... Bidders must score at least 70 out of 100 in respect of functionality in order to qualify for advancement" (ocds-9t57fa-165951). Scoring style is a 1–5 qualitative scale converted to weighted points: "1 = poor, 2 = average, 3 = good, 4 = very good, and 5 = excellent" (ocds-9t57fa-165951).
- Falling short is explicitly fatal and phrased as non-responsiveness, not merely a low score: "A bidder that scores less than 70 out of 100 will be regarded as submitting a non-responsive bid" (ocds-9t57fa-165951).
- The recruitment-agency RFB (ocds-9t57fa-165939) and all eight goods/plant-hire packs (ocds-9t57fa-165781, 164860, 165775, 164876, 165776, 164869, 165885) contain no functionality stage at all — evaluation there runs straight from mandatory documents to price/B-BBEE (Phase 1 → Phase 2/Administrative → price+preference), so a 70/100 functionality cut is a services-RFB feature, not a department-wide default.

## Distinctive kill rules / quirks

- **Local content designation used as a hard specification gate, at 100%, for a category most buyers treat as a scored preference**: "Only locally produced or locally manufactured wood material from local raw material or input will be considered for this bid. The stipulated minimum threshold for local production and content for wood material Sector is 100%" (ocds-9t57fa-165781) — bidders below threshold must obtain a dtic exemption letter rather than simply losing points: "An exemption letter from the dtic must be obtained as per the exemption process followed by the dtic for items or materials that are imported and in cases whereby local content requirements cannot be met" (ocds-9t57fa-165781).
- **Undisclosed multi-company directorships are an automatic disqualifier at VOCMA**: "Bidders/ Individuals that are directors or members in more than one company bidding for this tender and do not openly declare their interests will be disqualified" (ocds-9t57fa-165951, 165939) — stricter/more specific than the generic SBD4 conflict-of-interest declaration used department-wide.
- **VAT non-declaration is a named, standalone disqualifier** in the VOCMA packs, separate from the general non-responsiveness rules: "Bidders who are registered for VAT who submit bids without VAT will be disqualified" (ocds-9t57fa-165939).
- **Evidence of cross-pack boilerplate/copy-paste artifacts**: the dump-truck-hire SCC's insurance clause still refers to "the pump and equipment" ("Delivery and documents 10.1 The pump and equipment will be delivered to the designated store yard at the site," ocds-9t57fa-164860) despite the contract being for a dump truck, and the ready-mix-concrete pack cites "The General Conditions of Contract SAICE 2010 Edition" (ocds-9t57fa-164876) where every other sampled pack cites "General Conditions of Contract (National Treasury 2010)" (e.g. ocds-9t57fa-165781) — worth flagging to a bidder as a buyer that reuses templates across dissimilar commodities without always scrubbing them.
- **Compulsory site briefings are used selectively and are fatal when set**: the Ntabelanga Dam materials packs require attendance as a Phase 1 mandatory item with GPS coordinates given ("Venue: Ntabelanga dam, Access Road close to Maclear in Eastern Cape Province Co-ordinates: 31˚07'19.2''S, 28˚40'59.1''E," ocds-9t57fa-165781) while the Paarl-based plant-hire and VOCMA services packs carry no briefing at all — bidders cannot assume briefing (or its absence) from one DWS tender to the next.
